text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: GPU node gpu-45 OOM + illegal memory access on serving-runtime. container serving-runtime-12 exited with code 1. Logs attached.

maria: seeing a spike in OOMs and then immediate cudaIllegalMemoryAccess. A few nodes flapped. Impact: ~2% of requests 503 in EU cluster.

ajay: oncall here. pulling logs now. Which model/route?

maria: route /v1/generate using rdx-llama-13b-8bit on dedicated-pool-eu-2. Pod restarted 3x in 5m.

ben: repro stack from kube:
```
stderr: CUDA error: illegal memory access
stack: serving/runtime/loader.cc:234: kv_cache_write -> segfault
container exit 1
```

liz: suspected pattern: heavy concurrent long-context requests -> eviction -> pagewalk thrash -> misaligned device addr in kernel. Could be kernel driver or our allocator.

ajay: node gpu-45 shows dmesg with "GPU: page fault at 0x7ff... illegal address". Starting node cordon/evac.

ops-bot: cordon/gpu-45 initiated by ajay

maria: customer-impact: A handful of customers reporting errors on long prompts (30k tokens). CS tracking ticket CS-9871.

customer-success: pinged customers in the affected cohort, offering retry guidance and ETA for fix.

ajay: mitigation steps I'm trying: 1) reduce max_context to 8k via route override for that model 2) scale down concurrent streams to 8 3) fallback to rdx-llama-13b-16bit on same pool.

ben: hotfix: rolled a patch to runtime allocator to add bounds-check in kv_cache_write, deployed to canary nodes (gpu-canary-2)

maria: canary build logs look ok for 30m. No illegal access reproductions yet. Traffic routed 5% to canary.

liz: also bumped kernel driver to nv-kernel-510 on canary for comparison.

ajay: after canary success, draining gpu-45 and rebooting node to clear SMMU mappings. Will evac pods to gpu-47/49.

ops-bot: drain gpu-45 started

sre-shadow: monitoring metrics: cuda_illegal_count fell to 0 on canary. overall 503s decreased to 0.5%.

ajay: full rollout: patch + kernel bump to pool nodes in EU. Rolling update in progress, 2min between nodes.

ben: note: put a temporary automatic fallback policy in routing to send long prompts to host-pool (higher latency) if container fails more than 2x in 10m.

maria: CS update: informed customers of mitigation, asked to escalate if they see further 500s.

customer-success: added note to CS ticket CS-9871: throttle long queries and suggest shorter context until fully rolled.

liz: root cause hypothesis: under heavy KV cache eviction, our allocator issues a device pointer with uninitialized offset leading to misaligned access in next kernel launch. Kernel driver's pagewalk exposes it as illegal memory access instead of clean trap. Repro requires high concurrency + long sequences.

ajay: next steps: 1) keep fallback active for 6 hours 2) schedule deeper repro with heap sanitizer on offline test 3) prepare kernel repro VM for NVIDIA with minimal C repro.

maria: time estimates: rollout completes in 20m, monitor 2 hours, then unpin fallback if stable.

sre-shadow: logging note: added extra KV allocation traces to runtime for 48h.

ben: retrospective TODOs: add unit tests for kv cache alignment, add allocator guard pages in debug builds, and add an autoscaling knob to limit concurrent long-context requests.

ajay: thanks all, will uncordon when healthy. If any new 500s, @maria and @ben please escalate.

maria: :thumbsup: closing initial incident thread, continuing postmortem separately. Incident severity: Sev2. Customer impact: limited but visible on long prompts.

incidents-bot: Incident updated: state=mitigated, assignee=ajay, incident_id=INC-2026-045
